title: Completed normal form and weighted order at a projective point
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $r\ge0$, and $B=k[X_0,\ldots,X_r]$ with the grading by total degree [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ be a prime ideal, $L=k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]_{\mathfrak p}$, and $N=\mathfrak pL$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Write $\delta(f)=f(1,t_1,\ldots,t_r)/1$, $U_d=\{f\in B_d:\delta(f)\in N^d\}$, and $U=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}U_d$. For any ideal $J$, write $\operatorname{ord}_J(h)=\sup\{n:h\in J^n\}$, with value $\infty$ for membership in every power. Suppose $0\le e\le r$, $1\le q_1\le\cdots\le q_e$, and $c_{i\ell}\in k$ give a triangular presentation
$$\sigma_i=X_i^{q_i}+\sum_{\ell=i+1}^{r+1}c_{i\ell}X_\ell^{q_i},\quad X_{r+1}=X_0,\qquad U=k[\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_e],$$
where $q_i=1$ in characteristic zero and the $q_i$ are powers of the characteristic otherwise. Set $\rho_i=\delta(\sigma_i)$, $\Delta=\{\beta\in\mathbf N^e:0\le\beta_i<q_i\}$, and $L_0=k[t_{e+1},\ldots,t_r]_{\mathfrak p\cap k[t_{e+1},\ldots,t_r]}$ with maximal ideal $N_0$. Denote maximal-ideal completions by hats [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. There exist $a_i\in L_0$, $h\ge0$, $\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_h\in N_0$, and a field $F\subset\widehat L_0$ such that $z_i=t_i-a_i\in N$, and the induced inclusions and continuous isomorphisms identify
$$\widehat L_0=F[[\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_h]],\qquad \widehat L=F[[\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_h,z_1,\ldots,z_e]].$$
Here power series have their usual coefficientwise meaning [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], the displayed variables generate the respective maximal ideals, and $F\to L_0/N_0\to L/N$ is an isomorphism. The natural map $L\to\widehat L$ is injective and preserves orders: $\operatorname{ord}_N(u)=\operatorname{ord}_{N\widehat L}(u)$ for $u\in L$. Every $v\in\widehat L$ has a unique convergent expansion
$$v=\sum_{A\in\mathbf N^e,\,\beta\in\Delta,\,\gamma\in\mathbf N^h}v_{A\beta\gamma}\rho^Az^\beta\omega^\gamma,\qquad v_{A\beta\gamma}\in F,$$
and
$$\operatorname{ord}_{N\widehat L}(v)=\min\{q\cdot A+|\beta|+|\gamma|:v_{A\beta\gamma}\ne0\},\qquad q\cdot A=\sum_iq_iA_i,$$
with minimum of the empty set $\infty$. Let $\epsilon_0:k\hookrightarrow F$ be the homomorphism obtained by reducing $k$ to $L_0/N_0$ and inverting the residue isomorphism of $F$. For a weighted homogeneous polynomial $P(S_1,\ldots,S_e)\in k[S]$ of weight $d$, where $S_i$ has weight $q_i$, write $P^{\epsilon_0}$ for its coefficient image. Then
$$P(\rho)-P^{\epsilon_0}(\rho)\in(N\widehat L)^{d+1}.$$
No containment of the original copy of $k$ in $F$ is asserted. Empty variable tuples are included.

source.place: External source read online: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10-1 (1970), Lemma 14 and (14.1)-(14.2), p.169; Remarks (16.1)-(16.2), pp.171-172. https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival copy WANTED; the ILO document is the VIII 2.3.13 ancestor motivation only. No Stacks tag states this specialized assertion.

proof.text: For $1\le j\le e+1$, put $R_j=k[t_j,\ldots,t_r]_{\mathfrak p\cap k[t_j,\ldots,t_r]}$ and let $M_j$ be its maximal ideal; thus $R_{e+1}=L_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring], these rings and $L$ are Noetherian regular local. Localizing first the suffix coefficients and then the remaining variables identifies $L$ with a localization of $R_j[t_1,\ldots,t_{j-1}]$ at a prime contracting to $M_j$. The denominators on both sides are exactly those inverted by localization at $\mathfrak p$. By [lem-trf-polynomial-localization-order-reflection], $N^a\cap R_j=M_j^a$ for every $a$. Since $\sigma_j\in U_{q_j}$, we obtain $\rho_j\in M_j^{q_j}$ for $j\le e$.

source.place: Lemma 14, proof, p.169: suffix local rings and contraction of powers; explicit application of the generic polynomial-localization lemma.

proof.text: Write $K_{j+1}=R_{j+1}/M_{j+1}$. The quotient $R_j/M_{j+1}R_j$ is $K_{j+1}[t_j]_{Q_j}$ for a prime $Q_j$. The image $g_j$ of $\rho_j$ is monic of degree $q_j$ and belongs to $(Q_jK_{j+1}[t_j]_{Q_j})^{q_j}$. It is nonzero and nonunit, so $Q_j\ne0$. By [lem-pur-polynomial-field-pid], write $Q_j=(f_j)$ with $f_j$ monic irreducible. Membership of $g_j$ in the localized power implies $f_j^{q_j}\mid g_j$ in the polynomial ring: a denominator outside $(f_j)$ is coprime to $f_j$, so Bezout cancels it successively. Thus $q_j\deg f_j\le\deg g_j=q_j$, whence $f_j=t_j-b_j$ for $b_j\in K_{j+1}$. Consequently $R_j/M_j=K_{j+1}$ by the natural map. Applying this for $j=e,e-1,\ldots,1$ proves $L_0/N_0\xrightarrow{\sim}L/N$.

source.place: Lemma 14, proof, p.169. Degree-versus-order calculation in the one-variable closed fibre; the PID input is Stacks Tag 030A (lemma-polynomial-domain-normal), field case.

proof.text:
Choose $a_i\in L_0$ lifting the residue of $t_i$ under the preceding residue isomorphism and put $z_i=t_i-a_i$. In $L_0[t_1,\ldots,t_e]$, the prime defining $L$ contains $(N_0,z_1,\ldots,z_e)$, whose quotient is the field $L_0/N_0$. Hence that prime equals this maximal ideal. Translation of the variables therefore identifies
$$L=(L_0[z_1,\ldots,z_e])_{(N_0,z_1,\ldots,z_e)}.$$
The identification fixes $L_0$, and each $z_i$ lies in $N$.

source.place: After Lemma 14, p.169, choice of lifts and (14.1).

proof.text: Choose a regular system of parameters $\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_h$ of $L_0$, so $h=\dim L_0$ and $N_0=(\omega)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local] and [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension], $\widehat L_0$ is Noetherian regular local of dimension $h$, with maximal ideal $N_0\widehat L_0$; by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-noetherian-quotient-noetherian] it is $N_0\widehat L_0$-adically complete. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-coefficient-ring-exists] to it: it gives a coefficient ring $\Lambda\subseteq\widehat L_0$ with maximal ideal $p\Lambda$, $p$ the characteristic of $L_0/N_0$, mapping isomorphically onto $L_0/N_0$. Since $k\subset L_0$, this characteristic is that of $k$: if it is $0$, $\Lambda$ is a field; if it is $p>0$, then $p=0$ in $\widehat L_0$, so $p\Lambda=0$ and again $\Lambda$ is a field. Let $c:L_0/N_0\to\widehat L_0$ be the inverse residue isomorphism followed by inclusion, a section of the residue map, and set $F=c(L_0/N_0)=\Lambda$. Apply [lem-trf-parameter-chart-completion-substitution] with $R=L_0$, parameters $\omega$, $r=e$ and $J=\varnothing$ to the ring in Step 3. It gives the continuous coordinate isomorphisms $\widehat L_0=F[[\omega]]$ and $\widehat L=F[[\omega,z]]$, with their stated parameter images and coefficient inclusion. The induced map between completions is inclusion of the $\omega$ variables and coefficients, hence is injective. The field maps on residues are those of Step 2.

source.place: (14.1)-(14.2), p.169; Cohen structure is used only for a coefficient section. Stacks Tags 07NY, 07NV, 05GH, 032A and 0C0S via the cited nodes.

proof.text: The maximal ideal of $L$ is finitely generated, since $L$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power], the map $L\to\widehat L/(N\widehat L)^a$ is the quotient map $L\to L/N^a$ for every $a\ge1$. Thus $u\in N^a$ if and only if its completed image lies in $(N\widehat L)^a$, and the two orders agree, including infinite order. The kernel of $L\to\widehat L$ is $\bigcap_aN^a$, which is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson], with module $L$ and ideal $N$ contained in the Jacobson radical of the local ring. This proves injectivity.

source.place: Remark (16.2), p.172, parenthetical order equality; Stacks Tags 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated) and 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module).

proof.text:
In the coordinates of Step 4, put $\mathfrak m=(\omega,z)$. Additivity of the $q_i$-th power in positive characteristic (and $q_i=1$ in characteristic zero) gives
$$\rho_i=z_i^{q_i}+\sum_{i<\ell\le e}c_{i\ell}z_\ell^{q_i}+b_i,\qquad b_i\in L_0.$$
Here $b_i=a_i^{q_i}+\sum_{i<\ell\le e}c_{i\ell}a_\ell^{q_i}+\sum_{e<\ell\le r}c_{i\ell}t_\ell^{q_i}+c_{i,r+1}$. Since $\rho_i\in\mathfrak m^{q_i}$ and all displayed $z$ terms have that order or higher, $b_i\in\mathfrak m^{q_i}$. Setting $z=0$ gives $b_i\in(\omega)^{q_i}F[[\omega]]$. An element of $(\omega,z)^n$ is exactly a series with no terms of total degree below $n$: one implication follows by multiplication, and conversely group each monomial of degree at least $n$ by a chosen degree-$n$ divisor, obtaining a finite sum of degree-$n$ monomials times series. Hence the degree-$q_i$ form of $\rho_i$ is
$$H_i=Z_i^{q_i}+\sum_{i<\ell\le e}\epsilon_0(c_{i\ell})Z_\ell^{q_i}+B_i(W),$$
where $B_i$ is homogeneous of degree $q_i$. Coefficients $c_{i\ell}$ may have higher $\omega$ terms; only their residues enter $H_i$.

source.place: (13.2), p.168, (14.2), p.169 and Remark (16.2), p.172; explicit initial homogeneous forms.

proof.text: For each $n$, the forms $H^AZ^\beta W^\gamma$ with $q\cdot A+|\beta|+|\gamma|=n$ are a basis of the degree-$n$ homogeneous polynomials in $(Z,W)$. Indeed, order degree-$n$ monomials lexicographically with $Z_1>\cdots>Z_e>W_1>\cdots>W_h$. The leading monomial of $H_i$ is $Z_i^{q_i}$ with coefficient $1$; therefore the leading monomial of $H^AZ^\beta W^\gamma$ is $Z^{qA+\beta}W^\gamma$, with coefficient $1$. The componentwise Euclidean divisions $D_i=q_iA_i+\beta_i$, $0\le\beta_i<q_i$, biject these triples with all degree-$n$ monomials. The change-of-coordinates matrix on this finite ordered set is triangular with diagonal $1$: successive subtraction of the largest monomial gives spanning, and the largest monomial of a nonzero finite combination proves independence. This proves the claim without a freeness or division theorem. It also shows that the degree-$q_i$ form of $\rho_i$ is nonzero, so $\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak m}(\rho_i)=q_i$.

source.place: Remark (16.2), p.172, largest-exponent argument expanded degree by degree. The homogeneous triangular matrix is finite in every degree.

proof.text: Construct the coefficients of $v$ by successive total degrees. After degrees below $n$ have been subtracted, the remainder lies in $\mathfrak m^n$. Expand its degree-$n$ component in the basis of Step 7 and subtract the corresponding finite sum of $\rho^Az^\beta\omega^\gamma$. Its degree-$n$ component is exactly that basis expansion by Step 6, so the new remainder lies in $\mathfrak m^{n+1}$. Starting with $n=0$ constructs the required series; it converges because all terms added at stage $n$ lie in $\mathfrak m^n$, and the coefficientwise model $F[[\omega,z]]$ is complete and separated. If two coefficient families differ, choose the least weight where they differ; finitely many triples have that weight, and their nonzero combination has nonzero initial form by Step 7. Thus the families cannot yield the same series. The same argument at the least nonzero coefficient weight proves the displayed order formula. The all-zero family represents zero and has order $\infty$. With empty variable tuples the argument is unchanged (degree zero alone when all variables are absent).

source.place: (14.2), p.169, and Remark (16.2), p.172: formal basis obtained by the finite-degree triangular reduction, with convergence and uniqueness written out.

proof.text:
The composite $k\to L_0/N_0\xrightarrow{c}F$ is the required injective homomorphism $\epsilon_0$, since the residue of a nonzero field element is nonzero. For every $a\in k$, the elements $a$ and $\epsilon_0(a)$ of $\widehat L_0$ have the same residue, so their difference lies in $(\omega)\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Write the weighted homogeneous polynomial as $P=\sum_{q\cdot A=d}a_AS^A$. Then
$$P(\rho)-P^{\epsilon_0}(\rho)=\sum_{q\cdot A=d}(a_A-\epsilon_0(a_A))\rho^A\in\mathfrak m^{d+1},$$
since $\rho_i\in\mathfrak m^{q_i}$. The zero polynomial and $d=0$ are covered by the same computation. This proves the last assertion without requiring that the original copy of $k$ lie in $F$.

source.place: Remark (16.1), pp.171-172, the explicit coefficient-difference computation.
